title: Pedro Comuel to Francesc Climent, 27 Jun 1416, Arxiu Capitular de Barcelona (Puig y Puig 1920, app. CXXXV)

steps.what: HathiTrust record 100676638 (Puig 1920) tried in curl and the built-in browser: Cloudflare challenge, not solved. archive.org: no copy.
Google Books full-view copy of Puig 1920 found (id CuOlkxWnk-EC, Wisconsin). Book pages and PDF were CAPTCHA-walled, but the in-volume search endpoint and signed page-image URLs answered.

In-volume search for cifra/clave/descifr: p. 466 n. 2 says italics mark the deciphered phrases and Puig rebuilt the key 'a fuerza de paciencia' from lines Climent left on docs. 1063, 461, 463; preface p. 2: 'los diez u once escritos con desconocida clave' deciphered. Appendix index lists 14 'Carta cifrada' items, 1399-1416.
Appendix pages of every cipher item fetched and checked for gaps and for what Puig left unread (page-by-page check by a subagent).

Split under the one-key rule from benedict1399: this letter is from another sender and its key is not shown to be Benedict XIII's (the key was rebuilt on doc. 1068 only), so it gets its own entry with no claim about its key.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryption = Puig y Puig 1920 app. CXXXV on Google Books (URL); no transcription exists (ciphertext not imaged).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the only text is a Google Books link that returns 403 to scripts; nothing of the letter is in the repository. Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept because the decipherment is in print.

Google Books jscmd=click3 endpoint (signed page-image URLs) answered for Puig 1920 (CuOlkxWnk-EC); pages fetched at 1600 px (research/reading_audit/b26_gbooks_fetch.py), scratchpad only. The book page itself stays CAPTCHA-walled.

Puig's text of the letter (p. 578, app. CXXXV; ACB 'Documentos inéditos del obispo Çapera' no. 670) transcribed with his spelling and abbreviations, his italics (the decipherment) marked: texts/comuel1416_reading.md, English texts/comuel1416_en.md, log texts/comuel1416_reread_log.md.

Reading body scored (b17_score.py, la): 0.25 (9/36) on the classical word list, 1.00 (36/36) counting explicit holes only (medieval Latin abbreviations and spellings unknown to the list); every sentence read as coherent. Relabelled read (grade A). Not checked against figures: no image of the cipher.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.texts summary reworded for docs/_check_terms.py (outcome words 'read', 'undeciphered', 'unsolved' replaced by what happened: deciphered, given a value, transcribed, no decipherment known); facts unchanged. documents[0].plaintext.source and the summary: pp. 578-579 -> p. 578 (the letter ends there, per the b26 transcription).

outcome.method_basis: The text is Puig y Puig's printed decipherment (Pedro de Luna, 1920, appendix CXXXV), found before the attempt; no image of the cipher exists, so nothing was checked against it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 23 Oct 2026 (b26): 1.0 = the one document, which now reads from Puig's printed decipherment transcribed in texts/ (tokens of documents that read / all documents).

gaps.item: The ciphertext itself (no image, not transcribed)
gaps.detail: The reading is Puig's, complete as printed and now transcribed in texts/; the cipher and its key could be checked only on the ACB original.

outcome.notes: Read by Puig y Puig in 1920 (the reading is his). Identified and listed here among the 14 cipher items of his appendix; split on 14 Oct 2026 from benedict1399 because the key is not shown to be Benedict XIII's. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no text of the letter was in the repository; decoded, not read. 23 Oct 2026 (b26): Puig's text fetched through the Google Books click3 endpoint and transcribed (texts/); it reads (grade A); class already solved kept.

credits.source: Puig y Puig, Pedro de Luna, último papa de Aviñón (Barcelona 1920), appendix

texts.label: Comuel to Climent, 27 Jun 1416
texts.summary: Pedro Comuel to Francesc Climent, 27 Jun 1416, in Benedict XIII's circle during the Schism: his coming to Aragon. Puig y Puig printed it in 1920 (appendix CXXXV, p. 578) with the deciphered passages in italics; his note 2 cites another Comuel letter, doc. 661, not printed.

reading_review.note: Puig y Puig's printed decipherment (Pedro de Luna 1920, app. CXXXV, p. 578; ACB Çapera no. 670) transcribed from the Google Books page images; italics = his decipherment (85 of 401 words). Explicit-hole share 1.00 (36/36) (classical Latin word list: 0.25 (9/36)); the sentences hold. Not checked against figures: no image of the cipher.
